clue.text: Jump in outburst of emotion in cinema

indicators.note: the word for jump is placed inside the word for an emotional outburst

parts.note: a fit is a sudden outburst, as in a fit of rage
to leap is to jump

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up in a fit of feeling while watching a film.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLEAPIT is British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British term for a seedy old picture house, supposedly infested with fleas.

clue.text: In respect of tax revenues, one's in fine A state

indicators.note: the words for one's go inside the other letters

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
CAL is the abbreviation for California, a US state
I is one, so one's means one is: I + S

explanation.surface: Someone in good financial shape thanks to tax income.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray A in the held clue is an OCR artefact; the clue reads 'one's in fine state'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal describes matters of public revenue and taxation.

clue.text: Pain for listener disturbed by a repeated cheer

indicators.note: disturbed letters are jumbled
the single letter given by a is used twice

explanation.surface: A listener is upset by the same cheer being shouted again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, the organ used to listen.

clue.text: Close in on stalk on plant

parts.note: to pen something is to enclose it
a stem is a stalk
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to home in on the stem of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Penstemon is a garden flower with tubular blooms, also called beard-tongue.

clue.text: Most patient, suffering these evil INNE desires

indicators.note: suffering implies being put through distress, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Even the most patient person endures wicked cravings.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray INNE in the held clue is an OCR artefact; the clue reads 'these evil desires', defined here by desires.
explanation.definitionFit: Temptations are cravings for something, especially something wrong.

clue.text: Unpredictable fellow as rodent-catcher

indicators.note: a catcher holds something within, so the fellow's name surrounds the rodent

parts.note: Eric stands for any fellow, a man's name
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A man's unreliable reputation as a rat-catcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic behaves irregularly, so it cannot be predicted.

clue.text: Individual cycling round a long time

indicators.note: the last letter is cycled round to the front of the word

parts.note: a single individual is one

explanation.surface: A lone cyclist pedals around for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immensely long period of time.

clue.text: Tough fibre that is placed under battering device

parts.note: a battering ram breaks down doors
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.definitionFit: Ramie is a strong plant fibre from a nettle-like Asian shrub.

clue.text: Agrees fellow fighters will be needed after short time

indicators.note: the fighters come after the short time in the answer

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
allies are those who fight on the same side

explanation.surface: Comrades in arms are called upon after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be needed' is surface padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: If one account tallies with another, it matches or corresponds.

clue.text: Study closely-worded contract?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
dense prose is packed tightly with words

explanation.surface: Advice to read a tightly drafted legal agreement carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to shrink or compress, so to contract.

clue.text: Uplifting sort of entertainer?

parts.note: not a performer who cheers the audience up but one who literally lifts heavy weights in a circus act

explanation.definitionFit: A circus muscleman performs by hoisting great weights, literally lifting things up.

clue.text: Blokes eating left egg and fruit

indicators.note: the blokes take in the other letters as if consuming them

parts.note: blokes are men
O is shaped like an egg, a common crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: A group of men tucking into leftover eggs and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A large juicy fruit of the gourd family, such as a cantaloupe or watermelon.

clue.text: Firm in a street somewhere in Berks

indicators.note: the firm's abbreviation is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business located on a road somewhere in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berks is short for Berkshire, an English county; ASCOT is a town there famous for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse town lies in the county of Berkshire, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Drink with meal can give one wind, expert admitted

indicators.note: the word for wind lets the expert in, holding it inside

parts.note: to twine is to wind or coil
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A warning that a drink taken with dinner can cause flatulence, as an expert concedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can give one' is linking padding for the surface: the wind here is the verb (to coil, rhyming with 'find'), not a gust or flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary wine of modest quality served to accompany food at the table.

clue.text: Ferocious beast? Pet scrambled on top of building offering life-saving protection

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on another is above it

parts.note: a bull is a dangerous animal

indicators.note: scrambled letters are mixed up

parts.note: the roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: A fierce animal and a pet clamber over a rooftop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulletproof means able to resist bullets, so it protects lives.

clue.text: Experts whose knowledge is only skin-deep?

definitions.text: Experts whose knowledge is only skin-deep?

parts.words: Experts whose knowledge is only skin-deep?
parts.note: skin-deep usually means superficial, but here the specialists literally study the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Medical specialists in disorders of the skin, so their field truly is the skin.

clue.text: Understanding the convention?

definitions.meaning: to gather is to infer or understand, as in I gather you are leaving
an assembly or meeting of people

explanation.definitionFit: Gathering means inferring, and also an assembly of people.

clue.text: After beginning was first to be shocked

indicators.note: the word for was first is placed after the word for beginning

parts.note: a start is a beginning
to lead is to be first, so led means was first

explanation.surface: Someone who led from the start got a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means jolted by sudden surprise or alarm.

clue.text: Capturing personal enemy but showing no sign of urgency

parts.note: taking a piece in chess means capturing it
one's means belonging to oneself, personal
time is called the enemy, from the saying that time is the great enemy

explanation.surface: Seizing one's personal foe, yet without any hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting slowly and without hurry.

clue.text: Socialist with a heart in the clan

parts.note: someone kind is warm-hearted, having a heart
red is the colour of socialism, so a Red is a socialist

explanation.surface: A compassionate left-winger at the heart of the clan.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means related by blood, belonging to the same family group.

clue.text: One policeman? Get a second, free

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A policeman asks for a moment to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Canadian mounted police force, so one particular kind of officer.

clue.text: City's objection spreading across nearly all the country

indicators.note: the objection spreads out around the shortened country

indicators.note: the final letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon.

clue.text: People scaling hills quickly? They take only seconds

definitions.meaning: whimsically, people who run up hills
competitors who finish second, taking second place

explanation.definitionFit: Those placed second in a contest; whimsically, those who race uphill.

clue.text: Recall confirmation of acceptability being received by lady

indicators.note: the lady takes the confirmation inside her

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, stands for a lady
OK confirms that something is acceptable

explanation.surface: A woman receives approval and brings back memories.

clue.text: Avoid a work by Chopin maybe — not having piano, right?

parts.note: Chopin wrote a famous set of preludes
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A question about avoiding a Chopin piece that has no piano part.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape, so it means to avoid.

clue.text: Popular government suppresses this movement

indicators.note: the words keep the answer pressed down inside them, out of sight

explanation.walkthrough: The movement is musical, not political: a largo is a slow movement.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a largo is a slow, stately movement or passage.

clue.text: Boy in church troubling his rector?

indicators.note: troubling suggests disturbing, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A choirboy who gives his vicar trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a church choir, typically a boy treble.

clue.text: Tory trick

explanation.definitionFit: Short for Conservative, and also a swindle or deceit.

clue.text: Indignation when there's no say about ineffectual type being made leader

indicators.note: the ineffectual type is put at the front of the answer

parts.note: taken as written
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: Resentment when a useless person is promoted and nobody has a voice in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's' is a link; 'say' is the crossword stand-in for 'for example', and the surface's 'no say' (no voice) hides it.

clue.text: Piece in which artist gives way to one fantastic idea
